```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 7.5,
  fig.height = 4.6,
  dpi = 120
)
library(rgraphtool)

load_or_fallback_football <- function() {
  res <- tryCatch(football_network(), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (!is.null(res)) return(res)
  set.seed(43)
  n <- 60L
  b <- rep(1:5, each = 12L)
  el <- list()
  for (i in seq_len(n - 1L)) {
    for (j in (i + 1L):n) {
      if (stats::runif(1L) < ifelse(b[i] == b[j], 0.45, 0.03)) {
        el[[length(el) + 1L]] <- c(i, j)
      }
    }
  }
  g <- graph_add_edges(graph_create(n, directed = FALSE), do.call(rbind, el))
  list(graph = g, positions = sfdp_layout(g, groups = b, mu = 0.4, max_iter = 80L))
}

load_or_fallback_celegans <- function() {
  res <- tryCatch(netzschleuder_network("celegansneural"), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (!is.null(res)) return(res)
  set.seed(1)
  n <- 80L
  b <- rep(1:4, each = 20L)
  el <- list()
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    for (j in seq_len(n)) {
      if (i == j) next
      p <- if (b[i] == b[j]) 0.18 else if (b[j] == b[i] + 1L) 0.08 else 0.01
      if (stats::runif(1L) < p) el[[length(el) + 1L]] <- c(i, j)
    }
  }
  g <- graph_add_edges(graph_create(n, directed = TRUE), do.call(rbind, el))
  list(graph = g)
}
```

This article brings together the `football`, `celegans`, and `model_selection`
cookbook workflows, introducing flat and hierarchical (nested) stochastic block
models (SBMs) and minimum-description-length (MDL) model selection between
degree-corrected (DC) and non-degree-corrected (NDC) variants.

## 1. Flat SBM inference on the college football network

In a flat SBM, each vertex $i$ is assigned to a group $b_i \in \{1, \dots, B\}$,
and we minimize the exact microcanonical description length $\Sigma(A, b)$
combining the graph likelihood and the prior entropy of the partition and block
edge counts. `compare_blockmodels()` fits both degree-corrected and
non-degree-corrected models and computes the posterior odds ratio between them.

```{r football-fit, fig.height = 4.2}
football <- load_or_fallback_football()
g <- football$graph

set.seed(43)
comparison <- compare_blockmodels(g)
print(comparison$comparison)

state <- comparison$best_state
block_sizes(state)

pos <- football$positions
edges <- graph_edges(g)
groups <- match(block_membership(state), sort(unique(block_membership(state))))
colors <- grDevices::hcl.colors(max(groups), "Dynamic")

old_par <- graphics::par(mfrow = c(1L, 2L), mar = c(3.5, 3.5, 2.5, 1))
graphics::plot(pos, type = "n", xlab = "", ylab = "", axes = FALSE, asp = 1)
graphics::segments(pos[edges[, 1L], 1L], pos[edges[, 1L], 2L],
                   pos[edges[, 2L], 1L], pos[edges[, 2L], 2L], col = "grey82")
graphics::points(pos, pch = 19L, col = colors[groups], cex = 0.85)
graphics::title("Football network: inferred blocks")

counts <- block_edge_counts(state)
graphics::image(seq_len(nrow(counts)), seq_len(ncol(counts)), counts,
                xlab = "Block", ylab = "Block", main = "Block edge counts")
graphics::par(old_par)
```

## 2. Hierarchical (nested) SBM on *C. elegans*

Flat SBMs have a resolution limit proportional to $\sqrt{N}$ when $B$ grows.
The nested SBM resolves this by modeling the block multigraph recursively as
another SBM at higher levels $\ell = 1, 2, \dots, L$.

```{r celegans-nested, fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 6.2}
celegans <- load_or_fallback_celegans()
g_ce <- celegans$graph

set.seed(1)
nstate <- minimize_nested_blockmodel_dl(g_ce)
print(nstate)
nested_summary(nstate)

# Project a single vertex's group membership across every level of the hierarchy
v_id <- min(47L, graph_num_vertices(g_ce))
sapply(seq_len(nrow(nested_summary(nstate))) - 1L,
       function(l) nested_project(nstate, l)[v_id])

# Inspect level-0 group sizes as a flat block state
level0 <- nested_level_state(nstate, 0L)
block_sizes(level0)

plot_hierarchy(nstate, main = "C. elegans: nested SBM")
```

## 3. Degree-corrected vs. non-degree-corrected nested model selection

Using `compare_blockmodels(..., nested = TRUE)` evaluates whether empirical
degree heterogeneity warrants the degree-corrected microcanonical prior. On
networks with broad degree distributions (such as political blogs), the DC
nested SBM achieves a decisively lower description length; on nearly regular
networks (such as college football), the simpler NDC model is often preferred.

```{r nested-model-selection}
set.seed(1)
cmp_fb <- compare_blockmodels(football$graph, nested = TRUE, nruns = 3L)
print(cmp_fb)
cmp_fb$comparison
```

When network access to Netzschleuder is available, the same comparison runs on
`polblogs` (`1,490` blogs, `19,090` directed links):

```{r polblogs-selection, eval = FALSE}
polblogs <- netzschleuder_network("polblogs")
set.seed(1)
compare_blockmodels(polblogs$graph, nested = TRUE)
```
